web_evidence.title: The Woman in Cabin 10 | Book by Ruth Ware | Official Publisher Page
web_evidence.note: The publisher’s sustained Chapter 1 excerpt consistently narrates Lo’s actions, perceptions, and memories as “I.”

web_evidence.title: The Woman in Cabin 10 — Ruth Ware authorized extract
web_evidence.note: The author-hosted seven-page extract supplies continuous first-person narration by Lo across the opening scene.

web_evidence.title: The Woman In Cabin 10 Makes One Big Change From The Book. Why It Went There, And What The Author Thinks About It
web_evidence.note: In an interview, Ruth Ware explicitly calls Cabin 10 a first-person book and says readers remain inside Lo’s perspective throughout.

web_evidence.title: The Woman in Cabin 10 Study Guide | Literature Guide | LitCharts
web_evidence.note: The guide identifies the novel’s point of view as first person and separately notes interspersed emails, Facebook posts, and forum posts.

web_evidence.title: Ruth Ware | Extra Scene from The Woman in Cabin 10
web_evidence.note: Ware explains that a short section from Judah’s perspective was removed from the novel, resolving concern that an alternate narratorial section might remain in the published structure.

person_note: The Goodreads evidence repeatedly and unmistakably exposes Lo as the participating “I” narrator across action, perception, memory, and reflection. Authorized opening excerpts independently show the same narration, and Ruth Ware’s whole-book description explicitly says the novel remains inside Lo’s perspective throughout. Interspersed emails and online posts are subordinate documents rather than sustained alternate base narration; Ware also confirms that a planned Judah-perspective section was removed. No credible contrary evidence remains.
